questions.explanation: CN^- is a strong-field ligand; Ni^2+ (d8) undergoes dsp2 hybridisation, giving a square planar geometry.

questions.explanation: Rate doubling when [A] doubles means rate ∝ [A]^1, so the order with respect to A is one.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.explanation: A covalent bond is formed by the mutual sharing of electron pairs between atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.explanation: Electronegativity decreases down group 15; nitrogen is the most electronegative of them.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.explanation: Oxidation (loss of electrons) always occurs at the anode.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is more acidic?
questions.explanation: The phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance, so phenol is more acidic than ethanol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The strongest base in aqueous solution among the following is
questions.explanation: The +I effect of two methyl groups and hydration make dimethylamine a stronger base than the others; aniline is weakest due to resonance.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.explanation: Water has extensive hydrogen bonding, giving it a much higher boiling point than the other group 16 hydrides.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.explanation: Proteins are polymers built from amino acid monomers linked by peptide bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The number of sigma and pi bonds in a benzene molecule (C6H6) is
questions.explanation: There are 6 C-H sigma bonds, 6 C-C sigma bonds in the ring and 3 pi bonds, i.e. 12 sigma and 3 pi bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The IUPAC name of CH3CHO is
questions.explanation: CH3CHO has two carbon atoms and an aldehyde group, so it is ethanal.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.explanation: HCl is a strong acid, so [H+] = 0.01 M = 10^-2 M and pH = 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.explanation: The electronegativity difference makes the C-Cl bond a polar covalent bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.explanation: In an exothermic reaction heat is released, so ΔH is negative.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct order of the first ionisation enthalpy of carbon, nitrogen and oxygen is
questions.explanation: Nitrogen has a half-filled 2p^3 configuration, giving it the highest first ionisation enthalpy: N > O > C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The shape of the methane (CH4) molecule is
questions.explanation: Four bonding pairs around carbon with no lone pairs give a tetrahedral shape with bond angles of 109.5 degrees.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following undergoes an SN1 reaction most readily?
questions.explanation: SN1 proceeds through a carbocation; the tertiary carbonium ion from (CH3)3CBr is the most stable, so it reacts fastest.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The number of P-O-P bridges present in a molecule of P4O10 is
questions.explanation: P4O10 contains 6 P-O-P bridges linking the four phosphorus atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.explanation: 2 C2H5OH + 2 Na -> 2 C2H5ONa + H2, giving sodium ethoxide and hydrogen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The standard enthalpy of formation of an element in its most stable standard state is

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of physical adsorption?
questions.explanation: Physical adsorption arises from weak van der Waals forces, so it is reversible and not specific.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The van't Hoff factor (i) for K2SO4 in dilute aqueous solution, assuming complete dissociation, is
questions.explanation: K2SO4 dissociates into 2 K+ and 1 SO4^2-, giving i = 3 for complete dissociation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The SI unit of enthalpy is
questions.explanation: Enthalpy is a form of energy, so its SI unit is the joule (J).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: One faraday of electric charge is equal to
questions.explanation: One faraday equals the charge on one mole of electrons, about 96500 C mol^-1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Oxidation, in terms of electrons, means
questions.explanation: Oxidation is the loss of electrons; reduction is the gain of electrons (OIL RIG).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The number of moles present in 180 g of glucose (molar mass = 180 g/mol) is
questions.explanation: n = mass / molar mass = 180/180 mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The SI unit of molar conductivity is
questions.explanation: Molar conductivity = conductivity/concentration, giving the SI unit S m^2 mol^-1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For the sparingly soluble salt Ag2CrO4, the solubility product expression is

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is a transition element?
questions.explanation: A transition element has a partially filled d subshell in a common oxidation state; Fe qualifies, whereas Ca, Zn and Na do not.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The electronic configuration of copper (Z = 29) is
questions.explanation: The fully filled 3d10 4s1 arrangement is more stable for copper, so Cu is [Ar]3d10 4s1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to Le Chatelier's principle, an increase in pressure shifts a gaseous equilibrium towards

options.C: the side with fewer moles of gas
options.D: the side with more moles of gas

questions.explanation: Raising the pressure favours the direction that reduces the number of gas molecules, i.e. the side with fewer moles of gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The number of moles present in 58.5 g of sodium chloride (molar mass = 58.5 g/mol) is
questions.explanation: n = mass / molar mass = 58.5/58.5 mol.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The final electron acceptor of the electron transport chain in aerobic respiration is
questions.explanation: Oxygen accepts the electrons at the end of the mitochondrial electron transport chain and forms water.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The 'father of genetics' is
questions.explanation: Gregor Mendel is regarded as the father of genetics for his work on the laws of inheritance.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The greenhouse gas that contributes most to global warming is
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is the principal greenhouse gas responsible for global warming, although methane is more potent per molecule.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Water and dissolved minerals are transported through the
questions.explanation: Xylem conducts water and minerals upward from the roots in plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The rate of transpiration in a small leafy shoot is measured using a
questions.explanation: A potometer measures the rate of water uptake, which closely reflects the rate of transpiration.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The fruit of the pea plant is a
questions.explanation: The pea fruit develops from a superior monocarpellary ovary and splits along two sutures, so it is a legume (pod).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Apical dominance in plants is caused mainly by
questions.explanation: Auxin produced by the apical bud suppresses the growth of lateral buds, causing apical dominance.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The variety of living organisms present in a region is called
questions.explanation: Biodiversity refers to the variety and variability of living organisms and the ecosystems they form.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The first stable product of the C4 (Hatch-Slack) pathway is
questions.explanation: In C4 plants CO2 is first fixed onto phosphoenolpyruvate to give the 4-carbon oxaloacetic acid (OAA).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The dominant phase in the life cycle of a fern is the
questions.explanation: In pteridophytes such as ferns, the conspicuous and long-lived phase is the diploid sporophyte; the gametophyte is small and short-lived.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Which of the following is a micronutrient?
questions.explanation: Zinc is required in very small amounts and is therefore a micronutrient, unlike N, P and K.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the lysosome?

options.A: the site of aerobic respiration and ATP synthesis
options.B: an organelle containing hydrolytic enzymes for intracellular digestion
options.C: the site of photosynthesis in plant cells
options.D: the packaging and secretion of proteins and lipids

questions.explanation: the lysosome refers to an organelle containing hydrolytic enzymes for intracellular digestion.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Leghemoglobin, which protects the nitrogenase enzyme, is present in
questions.explanation: Leghemoglobin occurs in the root nodules of legumes and keeps the nodule interior anaerobic, protecting nitrogenase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The type of placentation in which ovules are borne on a single placenta along the ventral suture, as in pea, is
questions.explanation: In marginal placentation the ovules are arranged in two rows on the ventral suture, as in pea.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The phenotypic ratio obtained in the F2 generation of a dihybrid cross is
questions.explanation: Mendel's dihybrid cross gives the F2 phenotypic ratio 9:3:3:1.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: In the Calvin cycle, the first stable product is
questions.explanation: Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase fixes CO2 onto RuBP, and the first stable product is 3-phosphoglyceric acid (3-PGA).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The double-helix model of DNA was proposed by
questions.explanation: James Watson and Francis Crick proposed the double-helix model of DNA in 1953.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The deficiency of magnesium in plants typically causes
questions.explanation: Magnesium is a central atom of chlorophyll; its deficiency causes chlorosis between the veins (interveinal chlorosis).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The plant hormone that promotes cell division (cytokinesis) is
questions.explanation: Cytokinins promote cell division and are synthesised in regions of rapid division such as root tips.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The logistic growth equation for a population is
questions.explanation: Logistic growth is described by dN/dt = rN(K - N)/K, where K is the carrying capacity.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the nucleolus?

options.A: the site of ribosomal RNA synthesis
options.B: a cytoplasmic channel connecting adjacent plant cells
options.C: the membrane surrounding the plant cell vacuole
options.D: an organelle involved in photorespiration and fatty-acid breakdown

questions.explanation: the nucleolus refers to the site of ribosomal RNA synthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the Golgi apparatus?

options.A: the packaging and secretion of proteins and lipids
options.B: the site of photosynthesis in plant cells
options.C: the site of ribosomal RNA synthesis
options.D: the site of aerobic respiration and ATP synthesis

questions.explanation: the Golgi apparatus refers to the packaging and secretion of proteins and lipids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Palisade parenchyma is a part of the
questions.explanation: Palisade and spongy parenchyma together form the mesophyll of a leaf.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The plant hormone responsible for cell elongation and phototropism is
questions.explanation: Auxin (IAA) promotes cell elongation and mediates phototropism by unequal distribution on the shaded side.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: According to the ten per cent law, the energy transferred from one trophic level to the next is about
questions.explanation: Lindeman's ten percent law states that only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level is transferred to the next.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The number of NADH molecules produced per glucose molecule during the Krebs cycle is
questions.explanation: Each turn of the Krebs cycle yields 3 NADH; one glucose gives two turns, so 6 NADH are produced.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The genetic material in most organisms is
questions.explanation: DNA is the genetic material in the vast majority of organisms, although some viruses use RNA.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Which group of plants is called the 'amphibians of the plant kingdom'?
questions.explanation: Bryophytes need water for the movement of male gametes to the egg, so they are called amphibians of the plant kingdom.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The genotypic ratio obtained in the F2 generation of a monohybrid cross is
questions.explanation: A monohybrid cross gives the genotypic ratio 1 (homozygous dominant) : 2 (heterozygous) : 1 (homozygous recessive).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The cohesion-tension theory explains the ascent of sap in the
questions.explanation: According to the cohesion-tension theory, water rises through the xylem due to transpiration pull, cohesion and adhesion.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the ribosome?

options.B: the site of aerobic respiration and ATP synthesis
options.C: the packaging and secretion of proteins and lipids
options.D: an organelle containing hydrolytic enzymes for intracellular digestion

questions.explanation: the ribosome refers to the site of protein synthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The fleshy edible part of a mango fruit is the
questions.explanation: The mango is a drupe whose fleshy edible portion is the mesocarp.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the mitochondrion?

options.A: the site of ribosomal RNA synthesis
options.B: an organelle involved in photorespiration and fatty-acid breakdown
options.C: the site of photosynthesis in plant cells
options.D: the site of aerobic respiration and ATP synthesis

questions.explanation: the mitochondrion refers to the site of aerobic respiration and ATP synthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Double fertilisation is a characteristic feature of
questions.explanation: Double fertilisation (syngamy and triple fusion) is found only in angiosperms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: In a parasitic food chain, the pyramid of numbers is
questions.explanation: A single host can support a large number of parasites, so the pyramid of numbers in a parasitic food chain is inverted.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Casparian strips are found in the
questions.explanation: The endodermal cell walls bear casparian strips (suberised bands) that block the apoplastic pathway in roots.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The process by which mRNA is synthesised from a DNA template is called
questions.explanation: Transcription is the synthesis of RNA from a DNA template.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The enzyme that unwinds the DNA double helix during replication is
questions.explanation: Helicase unwinds the DNA double helix at the replication fork.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: In a DNA double helix, adenine pairs with
questions.explanation: A pairs with T through two hydrogen bonds and G pairs with C through three hydrogen bonds.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The net gain of ATP molecules by substrate-level phosphorylation during glycolysis of one glucose molecule is

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the chloroplast?

options.A: the site of ribosomal RNA synthesis
options.B: an organelle involved in photorespiration and fatty-acid breakdown
options.C: the membrane surrounding the plant cell vacuole
options.D: the site of photosynthesis in plant cells

questions.explanation: the chloroplast refers to the site of photosynthesis in plant cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: A vascular bundle in which the cambium is present is called
questions.explanation: The presence of cambium between xylem and phloem makes a bundle open, allowing secondary growth.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The producers of an ecosystem are
questions.explanation: Green plants (autotrophs) trap solar energy and form the base of every food chain.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The light reaction of photosynthesis takes place in the
questions.explanation: The photosystems and electron carriers of the light reaction are embedded in the thylakoid membrane.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The association between an alga and a fungus in a lichen is an example of
questions.explanation: In a lichen the alga photosynthesises and the fungus provides shelter and minerals, so both benefit (mutualism).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The hormone secreted by the corpus luteum is
questions.explanation: The corpus luteum mainly secretes progesterone, which maintains the uterine lining during the early stages of pregnancy.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Fertilisation in humans normally occurs in the
questions.explanation: Fertilisation normally takes place in the ampullary-isthmic junction of the fallopian tube.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The blood group regarded as the universal donor is
questions.explanation: O negative red cells carry neither A, B nor Rh D antigens, so they can be given to almost all recipients (universal donor).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes Porifera?

options.A: sponges with a water-canal system and spongin fibres
options.C: radially symmetrical animals bearing stinging cells (cnidoblasts)
options.D: flattened worms with flame cells for excretion

questions.explanation: Porifera refers to sponges with a water-canal system and spongin fibres.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Bt cotton is resistant to insect pests because it carries
questions.explanation: Bt cotton expresses cry genes from Bacillus thuringiensis, whose protein is toxic to certain insect larvae.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The hormone that increases water reabsorption in the collecting duct is
questions.explanation: Antidiuretic hormone increases the permeability of the collecting duct to water, concentrating the urine.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The hormone that lowers blood glucose is
questions.explanation: Insulin, secreted by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans, lowers blood glucose by promoting its uptake and storage.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is used to
questions.explanation: PCR amplifies (makes many copies of) a specific segment of DNA using primers, a polymerase and thermal cycling.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Antibody-mediated immunity is also known as
questions.explanation: Antibody-mediated (B-cell) immunity acts through antibodies in the body fluids, so it is called humoral immunity.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Exchange of respiratory gases in the lungs occurs across the
questions.explanation: The thin, highly vascular walls of the alveoli are the actual site of gaseous exchange between air and blood.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Malaria is caused by
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium, transmitted by the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Erythroblastosis foetalis is likely to occur when

options.B: the mother is Rh-negative and the foetus is Rh-positive
options.C: both the mother and the foetus are Rh-negative
options.D: the mother is Rh-positive and the foetus is Rh-negative

questions.explanation: An Rh-negative mother sensitised to Rh-positive foetal cells produces antibodies that destroy the red cells of a subsequent Rh-positive foetus.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Bile juice helps mainly in the
questions.explanation: Bile salts emulsify fats, breaking large fat globules into smaller droplets so that lipases can act on them.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes Arthropoda?

options.A: soft-bodied animals usually with a calcareous shell and a mantle
options.B: spiny-skinned animals with a water-vascular system
options.C: a phylum of worm-like animals with a stomochord
options.D: the largest phylum, with jointed appendages and chitinous exoskeleton

questions.explanation: Arthropoda refers to the largest phylum, with jointed appendages and chitinous exoskeleton.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The enzyme pepsin acts in the
questions.explanation: Pepsin is a protease that acts in the acidic medium of the stomach, converting proteins into peptones.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes Platyhelminthes?

options.B: flattened worms with flame cells for excretion
options.C: the largest phylum, with jointed appendages and chitinous exoskeleton
options.D: worms with true metameric segmentation and a closed circulatory system

questions.explanation: Platyhelminthes refers to flattened worms with flame cells for excretion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes Aschelminthes?

options.A: worms with true metameric segmentation and a closed circulatory system
options.B: soft-bodied animals usually with a calcareous shell and a mantle
options.C: the largest phylum, with jointed appendages and chitinous exoskeleton

questions.explanation: Aschelminthes refers to roundworms possessing a pseudocoelom.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The number of bones in the adult human body is
questions.explanation: An adult human skeleton has 206 bones.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The theory of natural selection was proposed by
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin proposed the theory of natural selection in his book 'On the Origin of Species'.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The structural and functional unit of the nervous system is the
questions.explanation: The neuron is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The ten percent law of energy transfer was given by
questions.explanation: Lindeman (1942) proposed that only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level is transferred to the next.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The gap between two successive myelin sheaths along an axon is called a
questions.explanation: The unmyelinated gaps in a myelinated axon are called nodes of Ranvier, where saltatory conduction occurs.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The natural pacemaker of the human heart is the
questions.explanation: The sino-atrial (SA) node generates the impulses that set the rhythm of the heartbeat, so it acts as the pacemaker.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The non-living components of an ecosystem are called
questions.explanation: Abiotic components include physical and chemical factors such as light, temperature, water and minerals.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney secrete
questions.explanation: Juxtaglomerular cells release renin, which starts the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system that raises blood pressure.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The functional unit of contraction in a muscle fibre is the
questions.explanation: The sarcomere, the region between two successive Z-lines, is the functional unit of muscle contraction.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Oral contraceptive pills prevent pregnancy mainly by
questions.explanation: Combined oral pills contain hormones that suppress the release of gonadotropins, thereby preventing ovulation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The enzyme used to cut DNA at specific recognition sites is
questions.explanation: Restriction endonucleases recognise specific base sequences and cut DNA at those sites, producing sticky ends.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The male gamete in humans is the
questions.explanation: The spermatozoon (sperm) is the motile male gamete.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Most of the carbon dioxide is transported in the blood as
questions.explanation: About 70% of CO2 is carried as bicarbonate ions, about 20-25% as carbaminohemoglobin and the rest dissolved in plasma.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Alternative forms of the same gene are called
questions.explanation: Alleles are the alternative forms of a gene that occupy the same locus on homologous chromosomes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: AIDS is caused by
questions.explanation: HIV is a retrovirus that infects helper T-lymphocytes and causes AIDS.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The volume of air inspired or expired during normal breathing (tidal volume) is about
questions.explanation: Tidal volume is about 500 mL in a healthy adult; larger volumes are used during forced breathing.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The resting membrane potential of a neuron is maintained chiefly by the
questions.explanation: The Na+/K+ ATPase pump transports 3 Na+ out and 2 K+ in, maintaining the resting potential across the membrane.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes Cnidaria?

options.B: flattened worms with flame cells for excretion
options.C: worms with true metameric segmentation and a closed circulatory system
options.D: radially symmetrical animals bearing stinging cells (cnidoblasts)

questions.explanation: Cnidaria refers to radially symmetrical animals bearing stinging cells (cnidoblasts).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The ABO blood group system in humans is an example of
questions.explanation: The ABO system is controlled by three alleles (IA, IB and i) of a single gene, so it is an example of multiple alleles.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The pyramid of energy in an ecosystem is
questions.explanation: Energy decreases at each successive trophic level, so the pyramid of energy is always upright.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The joint between the humerus and the pectoral girdle is a
questions.explanation: The shoulder joint is a ball-and-socket joint, allowing movement in all planes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The 'master gland' of the human body is the
questions.explanation: The pituitary is called the master gland because it controls the secretion of many other endocrine glands.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The surgical method of permanent birth control in females is
questions.explanation: Tubectomy (tubal ligation) is the surgical sterilisation method used in females; vasectomy is used in males.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The interaction in which both interacting species benefit is called
questions.explanation: In mutualism both partners benefit, giving a (+/+) relationship, as in lichens and mycorrhizae.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes Annelida?

options.A: spiny-skinned animals with a water-vascular system
options.B: the largest phylum, with jointed appendages and chitinous exoskeleton
options.C: worms with true metameric segmentation and a closed circulatory system
options.D: soft-bodied animals usually with a calcareous shell and a mantle

questions.explanation: Annelida refers to worms with true metameric segmentation and a closed circulatory system.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The ozone layer protects living organisms from
questions.explanation: Stratospheric ozone absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun, protecting living organisms.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The structural and functional unit of the kidney is the
questions.explanation: Each kidney contains about a million nephrons, the units that filter blood and form urine.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The hormone that triggers ovulation is
questions.explanation: A surge of luteinising hormone (LH) around the middle of the cycle triggers the rupture of the mature follicle (ovulation).
